title: New chemiphotobleaching protocol for Raman spectroscopy
author: Elena Yakubovskaya
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bchqit5w

steps.title: Fix Cell Suspension
steps.instruction: Fix the cell suspension using formaldehyde.

substeps.instruction: Add formaldehyde to a final concentration of 2%.

steps.title: Concentrate Cells onto Membrane
steps.instruction: Concentrate the fixed cells onto GTTP 0.2 um membranes by filtering an appropriate volume based on cell density.

steps.title: Apply Hydrogen Peroxide
steps.instruction: Place the filter in a small petri dish and add 2 ml of 3% Hydrogen Peroxide.

steps.title: Perform Chemiphotobleaching
steps.instruction: Expose the petri dish containing the filter to bright white (3695) direct light (60 Lumens per Watt) using a regular desk LED light lamp.

substeps.instruction: Maintain a distance of 5-10 cm between the light source and the petri dish.

steps.title: Transfer Sample to Slide
steps.instruction: Transfer the bleached sample from the GTTP membrane to a mirror-finished stainless steel microscope slide.

substeps.instruction: Prepare filter wedges of GTTP membranes.
Place 5 ul sterile MilliQ water on a clean mirror-finished stainless steel microscope slide.
Wedge the sample side down onto the water.

steps.title: Freeze and Peel Membrane
steps.instruction: Freeze the sample to adhere cells to the slide and remove the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Place the mirror-finished stainless steel microscope slide and filter on a -80°C chilled aluminium block.
After ~20 sec, peel the membrane away, leaving cells frozen to the slide.
Return the slide to room temperature (RT) and air dry.

steps.title: Perform Raman Spectroscopy
steps.instruction: Perform Raman spectroscopy measurements on the prepared sample.
